summary: Stale-socket onclose race: heartbeat.reconnect() closes the old socket without nulling its onclose handler, so a delayed close event from the dead socket fires after a new socket is already connected, spawning an orphan/duplicate connection.
failure_scenario: Heartbeat pong-timeout fires (the socket is a half-open/black-holed TCP). reconnect() calls ws.close(), sets ws=null, and scheduleReconnect(500). Because the connection is dead, the OS delays the close handshake past 500ms. At 500ms connectWS() creates socket B and ws=B; B authenticates (auth_ok resets wsReconnectAttempt=0). Only then does socket A's still-attached onclose (line 3338, never nulled) fire: it clobbers sessionId=null (dropping B's live session), runs the unplanned branch wsReconnectAttempt++ and scheduleReconnect(2-5s), which then creates socket C and orphans socket B. B is still OPEN with its own onmessage/onopen closures, so messages get processed twice (only partly masked by id-dedup), typing ACKs double-fire, and when B eventually closes it schedules yet another reconnect.
suggested_fix: Capture the socket locally in connectWS (`const socket = new WebSocket(WS_URL)`) and early-return from onopen/onmessage/onclose when `ws !== socket`. Additionally, in heartbeat.reconnect (and shard_moved) null the old handler before closing, exactly as switchIdentity already does at line 2355 (`ws.onclose = null; ws.close();`).

summary: edit_message sends new_content to the channel WITHOUT redactSecrets, bypassing the credential mask that reply/thread_reply apply.
failure_scenario: An agent (or a prompt-injected agent) calls edit_message with new_content containing its `ac_...` key or a claim URL. reply (line 1652) and thread_reply (line 1712) both run redactSecrets before send, but edit_message forwards new_content verbatim over the WebSocket. The token becomes permanent, un-redacted channel content visible to every member — exactly the leak the server instructions forbid. delete_message is fine (no content) but edit is the redaction hole.
suggested_fix: Mirror the reply path: `const new_content = redactSecrets(await resolveBareMentions(chat_id, rawNewContent));` before building the WS frame at line 1739-1742.

summary: Add unit tests for HeartbeatMonitor.tick() covering all four readyStates plus pong-timeout and connect-timeout paths — this is already fully seam-injected yet has zero tests.
failure_scenario: A regression in tick() (e.g. flipping the WS_CONNECTING branch to reconnect immediately, or dropping the reconnecting guard) silently breaks dead-connection recovery: the plugin either never reconnects after a dropped socket or thrashes in a reconnect loop, and no test catches it. Concretely: getReadyState=WS_OPEN with lastPong older than pongTimeout must call reconnect exactly once; WS_CONNECTING for < connectTimeout must NOT reconnect but must after; WS_CLOSED must reconnect; a second tick while reconnecting must be a no-op.
suggested_fix: No refactor needed — HeartbeatDeps is already injectable. Write bun tests that construct `new HeartbeatMonitor({sendPing,reconnect,getReadyState}, ping, pong, connect)` with jest/bun fake timers or a manually-advanced Date.now stub, drive `receivedPong()` / `tick()` directly, and assert call counts on spy deps. Assert: (a) OPEN within pong window sends ping, (b) OPEN past pongTimeout reconnects and suppresses a second reconnect until resetReconnecting(), (c) CONNECTING respects connectTimeout, (d) CLOSING/CLOSED reconnect immediately.

summary: Add tests for recordOrSkipDeliveredMessage / messageDedupKey covering first-delivery, duplicate detection across sources, malformed messages, and the 5000-entry eviction that keeps the newest 4000.
failure_scenario: The live-WS + reconnect-backfill race relies entirely on this dedup Set. If eviction logic breaks (e.g. slice(1000) keeps the wrong half) a long-running agent past 5000 messages starts re-delivering old messages or dropping fresh ones, double-notifying Claude Code. Also messageDedupKey returns null when id/channel_id aren't strings, which must cause recordOrSkip to return false (never dedup) — untested. Feeding the same {id,channel_id} twice must return true the second time regardless of __source.
suggested_fix: Extract the dedup Set + MAX constant + the three functions into a small `dedup.ts` module (or export them from server.ts guarded so importing doesn't run main()). Because they close over module-scope `deliveredMessageIds`, add a `resetDeliveredMessages()` test hook or make it a class holding the Set. Then bun-test: first call false, second true, null-key false, and push 5001 unique keys asserting size drops to ~4000 and the oldest is evicted while the newest survive.

summary: Extract and test the @mention gate (isMentioned) — content.includes(`@${AGENT_ID}`) OR the `@displayName(agentId)` regex — including the false-positive it was patched to avoid.
failure_scenario: This is the exact code the comments (lines 3180-3184, msg:fc8b9b1a) say already caused a real bug: a system line like `User joined: name (acc_xyz)` matched the old loose `(<agentId>)` clause and the agent processed messages it wasn't mentioned in, eating context window. The tightened regex `@[^(\n]+\(${idEsc}\)` is untested, so a future edit could re-introduce the false positive, or break the true positive where the agent IS mentioned as `@Claude(my-id)`. Also idEsc escaping of a raw AGENT_ID containing regex metachars is untested.
suggested_fix: Extract a pure `isMentioned(content: string, agentId: string): boolean` helper (build displayMentionRe inside it) and call it from the handler. Then bun-test: (a) `@<agentId>` bare hit → true, (b) `@Name(<agentId>)` → true, (c) `User joined: name (<agentId>)` (no leading @Name) → false, (d) mention of a different id → false, (e) agentId with a `.` or `+` in it doesn't corrupt the regex.

summary: Add tests for redactSecrets covering ac_ API keys and JWT patterns, boundary lengths, and multiple occurrences in one string.
failure_scenario: redactSecrets is the last line of defense against leaking `ac_...` keys and JWTs into logs/messages (the MCP server instructions explicitly forbid leaking credentials). If the regex is weakened — e.g. the `{16,}` bound or the JWT three-segment pattern is edited — real keys pass through unredacted and are written to stderr or forwarded. Untested cases: an `ac_` key exactly 16 chars, a 15-char one that should NOT match a partial, two keys in one line (global flag), and a JWT with `-`/`_` base64url chars.
suggested_fix: Export redactSecrets (or move to a pure util module) and bun-test with fixtures: assert `ac_` + 20 chars → `ac_***REDACTED***`, a full `eyJ....` JWT → `***JWT_REDACTED***`, both present together both redacted, and that ordinary text containing `ac_` followed by <16 chars is left intact.

summary: Extract computeReconnectDelay(attempt) from ws.onclose and test the exponential-backoff cap plus the planned-reconnect (shard_moved) branch that resets the attempt counter.
failure_scenario: The reconnect delay `Math.min(wsReconnectAttempt * 2, 30) * 1000 + jitter` and the isPlannedReconnect early-return are embedded in the onclose closure, untestable. A regression that drops the `Math.min(...,30)` cap makes reconnect delay grow unbounded after many failures (agent goes permanently offline during an outage); a regression that forgets to reset wsReconnectAttempt=0 on planned shard_moved makes a rolling deploy push each successive hop 2s/4s/6s further out (the exact scenario documented at lines 3316-3321).
suggested_fix: Extract `computeReconnectDelay(attempt: number, rand = Math.random): number` returning the ms delay, and `nextAttemptAfterClose(attempt, isPlanned): number` returning the new attempt counter. Test: attempt 1..15 delays are capped at 30_000 + jitter, jitter is within [0,3000) with an injected rand, and a planned close returns attempt 0 while an unplanned one increments.

summary: bin ships raw TypeScript with a bun shebang while README tells users to run it via npx (Node).
failure_scenario: bin maps agentschat-mcp -> src/server.ts, whose first line is '#!/usr/bin/env bun'. README (lines 10 and 207) instructs `claude mcp add agentschat -- npx agentschat-mcp`. npx executes the bin under Node's resolver: on a machine without bun on PATH the shebang fails ('env: bun: No such file or directory'); on Windows npx ignores the shebang and invokes Node, which cannot parse the .ts syntax. Users following the documented install get a cryptic failure. engines.bun does not make npm/npx install or use bun.
suggested_fix: Ship a compiled JS build (bun build/tsup) with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang and point bin at the built file, OR change docs to `bunx agentschat-mcp` and add a runtime bun-presence check with a clear error message.

summary: Heartbeat 'fast' 500ms reconnect is silently downgraded to the 2-5s exponential backoff because the just-closed socket's unplanned onclose reschedules over the pending timer.
failure_scenario: heartbeat.reconnect() (line 3370) resets wsReconnectAttempt=0 and schedules a 500ms reconnect to recover quickly. But it does not set isPlannedReconnect, so when the old socket's onclose fires it takes the unplanned branch (line 3351): wsReconnectAttempt++ then scheduleReconnect(delay) where scheduleReconnect first does `if (reconnectTimer) clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)` (line 2995), cancelling the 500ms timer and replacing it with a 2000-5000ms one. Every heartbeat-forced reconnect therefore waits 2-5s instead of 0.5s, and the backoff counter is corrupted, defeating the stated 'faster recovery' goal.
suggested_fix: Have heartbeat.reconnect set a 'forced/planned' flag (or null the old onclose) so onclose does not increment wsReconnectAttempt and does not re-schedule over the intended 500ms timer — mirror the isPlannedReconnect handling used for shard_moved.

summary: knownChannels is only ever added to (never pruned on leave_channel), so it grows unbounded and backfillAllChannels does a sequential REST fetch per channel — including channels the agent has already left — on every auth_ok.
failure_scenario: channel_created adds ids at line 3311 but leave_channel (line 1994) removes nothing from knownChannels (nor from lastSeenMessageTs). A long-lived agent that joins/leaves many ephemeral channels (DMs, OKR channels, game channels) accumulates hundreds of dead ids. On every reconnect, backfillAllChannels (line 3020) iterates all of them, issuing a serial `GET /api/channels/:id/messages` for each — including left channels that now return 403/404 — turning each reconnect into an ever-slower O(all-time-channels) REST storm and leaking memory that grows for the process lifetime.
suggested_fix: On successful leave (line 2005/2010) and on WS leave fallback, call knownChannels.delete(chat_id) and lastSeenMessageTs.delete(chat_id) + scheduleLastSeenMessageTsSave(). Optionally cap knownChannels size and rebuild it authoritatively from channel_created events each auth_ok.

summary: Cold-start / new-channel backfill uses `?limit=1` and re-injects that single latest message through handleWSMessage, so on a fresh start (or a newly joined channel) a stale DM/@mention is replayed as a live notification — contradicting the 'empty cursors = no backfill' contract.
failure_scenario: When lastSeenMessageTs has no cursor for a channel, backfill fetches `?limit=1` and, because dedupedReplay skips the `after` filter when `after` is falsy (line 3038), replays that one newest message through currentHandleWSMessage. On a genuine cold start deliveredMessageIds is empty, so recordOrSkipDeliveredMessage does not drop it. If that newest message happens to be a DM or an @mention, the agent emits a notifications/*/channel event and responds to a possibly hours-old message every time the process restarts without a persisted cursor file (first run, wiped config, or a channel joined mid-session). The code comment at line 3005 claims cold start does no backfill, but it does.
suggested_fix: When there is no cursor, seed lastSeenMessageTs from the fetched message's timestamp WITHOUT re-injecting it (skip the handleWSMessage replay for the no-cursor case), or fetch limit=1 purely to set the cursor and `continue`.

summary: The WebSocket-constructor-failure retry uses a raw untracked setTimeout(connectWS, 5000) that is not stored in reconnectTimer and not cleared on shutdown, so it can race with scheduleReconnect to open two sockets and can fire connectWS after shutdown.
failure_scenario: If `new WebSocket(WS_URL)` throws (transient DNS/URL error), line 3071 schedules an untracked 5s retry. Meanwhile any other path (onclose, heartbeat, shard_moved) may also call scheduleReconnect, whose reconnectTimer is a separate handle. Both timers fire connectWS independently, producing two concurrent sockets (the orphan-socket race in finding 1). The same untracked pattern applies to the auth_ok backfill timer at line 3121, which stacks multiple concurrent backfillAllChannels on rapid reconnects. Neither timer is cleared by shutdownFromStdio (line 3388 only clears reconnectTimer).
suggested_fix: Route the constructor-failure retry through scheduleReconnect(5000) so it shares the single tracked reconnectTimer, and track/clear the backfill timer id on shutdown and switchIdentity.

summary: mark_read sends a read_receipt WS frame with last_read_id before validating it, then calls last_read_id.slice(0,8) which throws TypeError when the arg is omitted — after the malformed frame is already on the wire.
failure_scenario: An agent (or client) calls mark_read({chat_id}) without last_read_id. Args are never runtime-validated (handler casts `args as any`; there is no zod check — confirmed at line 1332). With WS open, line 2157 dispatches `{type:'read_receipt', last_read_id: undefined, ...}` to the hub (a malformed/ambiguous cursor frame that may reset/clobber the server-side read cursor), then line 2161 `last_read_id.slice(0,8)` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`, surfacing as a tool error even though the side effect already fired. The identical unguarded-slice-after-dispatch pattern exists in set_topic (line 1849 `topic.slice(0,50)`), forward (line 1862 `target_channel_id.slice(0,8)`), and vote (line 1893 `proposal_id.slice(0,8)`).
suggested_fix: Validate required args before dispatching: `if (typeof last_read_id !== 'string' || !last_read_id) return {content:[{type:'text',text:'Error: last_read_id required'}]};` then send the frame. Apply the same guard to set_topic/forward/vote (topic, target_channel_id, proposal_id).

summary: Registration logs the full claim_url (which embeds the agent key) to stderr, inconsistent with the deliberately-masked banner at line 243.
failure_scenario: On first run the server returns data.claim_url of the form `${REST_URL}/chat/<id>?key=<agent-key>`. Line 167 writes it verbatim to stderr. Line 240-243 later takes pains to print `?key=<your-agent-key>` (placeholder) precisely to avoid this. stderr from an MCP plugin is captured in Claude Code / MCP host log files and terminal scrollback, so the ownership-granting credential lands in plaintext logs. Anyone with the claim URL can claim/control the agent.
suggested_fix: Do not print claim_url with the embedded key. Print the masked form (host + agent_id + `?key=<your-agent-key>` placeholder) consistently, or strip the query string before logging.

summary: redactSecrets only masks ac_ tokens and JWTs — it does NOT redact claim URLs, `?key=` params, passwords, or generic keys that the server instructions explicitly list as forbidden.
failure_scenario: The MCP server instructions say NEVER include 'API keys (ac_xxx), tokens, passwords, claim URLs' in message content, but redactSecrets (lines 1271-1274) covers only `ac_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}` and JWT shapes. An agent pasting a full claim URL whose key is not ac_-prefixed (or another service's password/API key) into a reply passes straight through to the channel. The named 'claim URL' credential class has no dedicated redaction at all — only the ac_ substring inside it would be caught.
suggested_fix: Add patterns for claim URLs (`/chat/[^?\s]+\?key=\S+` and any `[?&]key=\S+`) and, where feasible, common `password=`/`secret=`/bearer patterns; redact the whole query value, not just an ac_ substring.

summary: Inbound thread_reply frames are silently dropped: the WS message handler only processes data.type === "message", but the protocol declares thread_reply bidirectional (Server -> Client).
failure_scenario: Another agent posts a thread reply containing @<thisAgent>(id). The server broadcasts {type:"thread_reply", parent_id, channel_id, sender_id, content, ...}. handleWSMessage matches none of its branches (pong/auth_ok/message/channel_created/shard_moved/error), so the frame is discarded. The agent is never notified of the mention, no notifications/*/channel is pushed to Claude Code, and lastSeenMessageTs is never advanced for that channel — so the reconnect backfill cursor also skips it. Thread mentions are effectively invisible to this MCP client.
suggested_fix: Add a branch that normalizes inbound thread_reply into the same code path as message (e.g. treat data.type === "thread_reply" like a message for @mention detection / notification / cursor advance), or explicitly OR it into the `data.type === "message"` gate at line 3122.

summary: Typing acknowledgement is emitted as a real `message` frame carrying the sentinel content "__typing__" instead of the protocol's dedicated `typing` frame (type 8), polluting the persisted message stream.
failure_scenario: On every DM/@mention the plugin sends {type:"message", content:"__typing__", content_type:"text", ...} into the channel. The server persists it as a normal message (the code has to filter content === "__typing__" in get_history, backfill, and the mention-context fetch to hide it). Any spec-conforming client that does not know this private convention — the web UI, iOS app, or an SDK consumer built strictly against protocol.md — renders a literal "__typing__" message and stores it in history. The correct `typing` frame (already implemented for the send_typing tool at line 1688) is not used here.
suggested_fix: Replace the __typing__ message injection with the spec `typing` frame: ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:"typing", channel_id: data.channel_id, sender_id: AGENT_ID})). This removes the need for the three __typing__ filter sites as well.

summary: State-changing WS verbs (thread_reply, reaction, pin, edit_message, delete_message, set_status, set_topic, archive_channel, forward, vote, propose, mark_read) are sent over WebSocket only, with no REST fallback and no message_ack confirmation — the exact half-open-socket hazard that forced `reply` onto REST.
failure_scenario: The code comment at line 1653 states "WebSocket may be half-open after deploy" and routes `reply` through REST for reliability. But thread_reply/reaction/pin/etc. still gate on ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN and ws.send(). After a rolling deploy the socket can report OPEN while being half-open; ws.send() resolves locally, the tool returns "...dispatched", but the frame never reaches the server and no message_ack is ever awaited (there is no inbound message_ack handler at all). The user is told the action succeeded when it silently vanished.
suggested_fix: Either add a REST fallback for these verbs (as done for reply), or handle the protocol's message_ack (type 7) to confirm delivery before reporting success, or at minimum downgrade the success wording when no ack is received.

summary: Extract the pure bare-@-mention rewrite from resolveBareMentions and test longest-display-name-wins, regex escaping of member names, the CJK/Latin terminator class, and the already-paren'd no-op.
failure_scenario: resolveBareMentions rewrites outgoing `@Name` → `@Name(id)` so receivers' mention regex fires. Bugs here silently break cross-agent addressing: if longest-name ordering regresses, `@Claude` wins over `@Claude Code` at a shared prefix and the wrong agent is tagged; if terminator handling regresses, `@Name。` (CJK period) or `@Name,` isn't rewritten; if escaping regresses a member name containing regex metachars throws. All untested because the fetch is inlined.
suggested_fix: Split into `rewriteBareMentions(text: string, members: {agent_id,display_name}[]): string` (pure) called by resolveBareMentions after the network fetch. Bun-test the pure function: two members sharing a prefix pick the longer, a name with `.`/`(` is escaped not interpreted, `@Name` at end-of-string and before CJK/Latin punctuation both rewrite, `@Name(existing)` is left untouched, and text with no `@` returns unchanged.

summary: Add tests for normalizeTimestampForCursor covering before/after fractional-second padding, the 9-digit passthrough, and non-ISO passthrough.
failure_scenario: This function pads fractional seconds so backfill cursors compare correctly against server timestamps. If it regresses (wrong pad char per mode, off-by-one on the 9-digit guard), the `after=` backfill cursor either re-fetches already-seen messages every reconnect or skips the boundary message — the precise class of missed/duplicate delivery Task #119 exists to prevent. It's pure and trivial to test but untested.
suggested_fix: Export the function and bun-test: `...T00:00:00.123Z` with mode 'after' → `.123000000Z`, mode 'before' → `.123999999Z`, an already-9-digit fraction is returned unchanged, a string with no fractional part or a non-string returns as-is.

summary: Extract and test the backfill replay filter (self-message + __typing__ drop, and the after-cursor dedup that compares normalized timestamps).
failure_scenario: backfillAllChannels re-injects REST-fetched messages through the live handler. The filter must drop this agent's own messages (sender_id === AGENT_ID) and `__typing__` placeholders, and the `dedupedReplay` step must exclude messages at-or-before the `after` cursor. If this regresses, a reconnect replays the agent's own messages back to itself or re-delivers the boundary message, producing duplicate notifications — and the sort must keep chronological order so lastSeenMessageTs advances monotonically.
suggested_fix: Extract `filterBackfillMessages(msgs, agentId, after)` returning the sorted, deduped array. Bun-test: self messages and __typing__ removed; with an `after` cursor, messages whose normalized ts <= after are dropped and > after kept; output sorted ascending by timestamp; empty input and undefined-after (cold start) handled.

summary: Test profile-path resolution: profileNameToPaths sanitization + explicit-path detection, and resolveProfilePath env/CLI precedence (AGENTSCHAT_PROFILE > AGENTCHAT_PROFILE > --profile > --name > default).
failure_scenario: A regression in the precedence chain or in name sanitization loads the wrong profile file, so the agent connects with the wrong identity/token — or, because `nameToPath` falls through to the first candidate when none exist, writes a new profile to an unexpected path. Names with `/` are treated as explicit paths; names with unsafe chars are replaced with `_`. None of this is tested and it directly governs which credentials the plugin uses.
suggested_fix: These read process.env, cliArgs, and existsSync at module scope, so they can't be imported without side effects. Extract them into a `profile-paths.ts` module that takes `{env, cliArgs, existsSync, profileDirs}` as parameters (pure over injected deps). Then bun-test: `a/b.json` returns [`a/b.json`], `weird name!` → `weird_name_.json` under both dirs, and resolveProfilePath honors each precedence level with the others unset.

summary: No tests, no test script, and no CI despite code explicitly written 'for testability'.
failure_scenario: heartbeat.ts (lines 1-2, 72) advertises 'extracted for testability' and a public tick() 'Exposed for testing', yet there are zero *.test.ts/*.spec.ts files, no "test" script in package.json (scripts are only start/dev), and no .github/workflows. Regressions in reconnect logic (pong/connect timeouts), profile resolution, and the 70-branch tool dispatch ship with no automated verification; a broken branch is only discovered at runtime by an end user.
suggested_fix: Add a test runner (bun test), write unit tests for HeartbeatMonitor.tick() state machine and profile resolution, wire a "test" (and "typecheck") npm script, and add a GitHub Actions workflow running them on PRs.

summary: Single ~1400-line CallToolRequestSchema handler with ~70 chained `if (name === ...)` branches.
failure_scenario: The dispatch handler spans lines 1332-2727 as one function containing roughly 70 sequential `if (name === "...")` blocks (list_skills, okr_*, hidden_identity_*, docs, etc.). Every request linearly re-tests names, shared concerns (auth, fetch, error shaping) are copy-pasted per branch, and the function is far past any reviewable size — making it error-prone to edit and impossible to unit-test a single tool in isolation.
suggested_fix: Replace the if-chain with a `Record<string, (args) => Promise<Result>>` handler registry, grouping tools into modules (okr, docs, moderation, skills); the dispatcher becomes a lookup + shared wrapper.

summary: Error returns never set isError:true, so MCP clients treat every tool failure as a successful result.
failure_scenario: grep shows 0 occurrences of `isError` in server.ts. All failure paths (e.g. 2724 `okr_set_links failed`, 2725 `network error`, 2727 `Unknown tool`) return `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: '...error...' }] }` with no isError flag. Per MCP spec a tool result without isError is a success; a calling model/agent cannot programmatically distinguish a network failure or unknown-tool from a valid answer, so it may act on an error string as if it were data.
suggested_fix: Return `{ isError: true, content: [...] }` for all failure/exception branches (a shared error helper makes this uniform).

summary: 58 raw fetch() calls duplicate base URL, auth header, response parsing, and bespoke catch blocks.
failure_scenario: server.ts contains 58 `await fetch(` calls, each independently rebuilding `${REST_URL}/api/...`, `headers: { Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN} }`, `.text()`/`.json()`, an `if (!r.ok)` branch, and a per-tool `${name} network error: ...slice(0,120)` catch (23+ near-identical catch blocks). Any cross-cutting change (timeout, retry, auth refresh, error normalization, isError) must be edited in dozens of places and is already applied inconsistently (varying slice lengths 120/140/200, differing message prefixes).
suggested_fix: Introduce one `hubFetch(path, opts)` helper that injects base URL + auth, parses the body, and returns a normalized `{ ok, status, data, errorText }`; call it from every branch.

summary: Tool arguments are trusted via 47 `args as {...}` casts with no runtime validation.
failure_scenario: There are 47 `args as {...}` type assertions and no runtime schema validation (zod/ajv not used; inputSchema JSON is only advertised to clients, never enforced). A client that omits a required field or sends the wrong type passes the TS cast unchecked: destructuring of an undefined `args` throws before the branch's try/catch (surfacing as an opaque MCP internal error), or a missing id yields a malformed REST URL. Malformed input is not caught at the boundary.
suggested_fix: Validate args against a shared schema (e.g. zod) at dispatch entry, returning a structured `isError` result on validation failure, or at minimum guard required fields before use.

summary: channelBrief truncates the member list to the first 50 ids (memberIds.slice(0,50)) before the presence query, so online/offline is silently wrong for channels with >50 members — the same truncation-before-server-call class as the just-fixed list_channels bug.
failure_scenario: A channel has 80 members. channel_brief (and the join_channel brief that calls channelBrief at line 1984) requests presence only for members[0..49] at line 1932. `online` at line 1933 therefore omits every member past index 50; those members are reported as offline, and `members.online` count in the brief (line 1955) undercounts. Ordering of `membersData.members` is server-defined, so which members get dropped is arbitrary.
suggested_fix: Page the presence lookup (chunk memberIds into batches of 50 and merge the `presence` maps) instead of dropping everyone after the first 50, or pass the full id set and let the endpoint cap.

summary: get_history and list_channels clamp `limit` with Math.min(limit, N) but never coerce to a number or enforce a lower bound, so a string/negative/NaN limit is passed straight into the REST query string — unlike the sibling handler which uses Math.max(1, Math.min(Number(limit)||d, cap)).
failure_scenario: Args are unvalidated (`args as any`, no zod). If a client/LLM sends `limit:"abc"`, `Math.min("abc",100)` is NaN → get_history fetches `/messages?limit=NaN` (line 2313); if it sends `limit:-5`, the URL becomes `?limit=-5`. list_channels has the same gap at line 2197 (`Math.min(limit,500)`). Contrast list_reports_i_submitted at line 1830 which correctly does `Math.max(1, Math.min(Number(limit)||20, 100))`. Result is a malformed request the hub may 400 or mishandle, versus a clean clamp.
suggested_fix: Normalize consistently: `const capped = Math.max(1, Math.min(Number(limit) || DEFAULT, CAP));` and interpolate `capped` into the URL, in both get_history (line 2313) and list_channels (line 2197).

summary: search calls r.json() without checking r.ok, so any non-2xx response (400 bad query, 401, 500) is swallowed into a generic 'Search failed' with no status, and an undefined `query` is sent as the literal string 'undefined'.
failure_scenario: search({}) with no query builds `new URLSearchParams({q: query})` at line 1870 → `q=undefined` sent to the server. If the endpoint returns 400/500 (or an HTML error body), `await r.json()` at line 1873 throws, dropping into the bare `catch` (line 1881) that returns only 'Search failed' — the agent gets no status code and cannot tell auth failure from a bad query. Every other handler in this file reports `(${r.status})`.
suggested_fix: Guard the arg (`if (!query || typeof query !== 'string') return error`) and check `if (!r.ok) return {..., text: \`search failed (${r.status})\`}` before parsing JSON.

summary: normalizeTimestampForCursor pads fractional-second timestamps to 9 digits but leaves whole-second timestamps (no '.') unchanged, so lexical comparison between the two formats is wrong ('.'=0x2E < 'Z'=0x5A), corrupting the backfill dedup/advance cursor when the server mixes formats.
failure_scenario: Cursor stored as `2026-06-30T12:00:00Z` (whole second, returned unchanged at line 2805), incoming backfill message at `2026-06-30T12:00:00.500Z` (padded to `.500000000Z`). At line 3042 the check `msgTs > afterTs` compares `...00.5...Z` vs `...00Z`: after the common prefix `...00`, `.` (0x2E) < `Z` (0x5A), so the fractional message sorts LESS than the whole-second cursor and is dropped as already-seen — a genuinely-missed message is never delivered. The same lexical compare drives the monotonic cursor advance at lines 3168-3171, which can then stick. Also, two messages sharing an identical timestamp (strict `>`) collapse to one delivery regardless of id.
suggested_fix: Normalize BOTH operands to a canonical form before comparing — either always inject a fractional part (`.000000000`) when absent, or parse to epoch-millis and compare numerically rather than lexically.

summary: The ac_ redaction regex `ac_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}` breaks on base64url tokens containing `-`/`_` and misses tokens shorter than 16 chars, leaking token fragments.
failure_scenario: If the agent key is `ac_` followed by a base64url body containing `-` or `_`, the character class `[A-Za-z0-9]` stops matching at the first special char, so any trailing segment of the token after that char is emitted un-redacted into channel content. A token whose alnum run is under 16 chars is not matched at all. Redaction thus gives a false sense of safety for real token formats.
suggested_fix: Broaden the class to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{12,}` (base64url-aware) and lower the minimum length to match the real key length; validate against an actual sample key format.

summary: set_status broadcasts status_text/status_emoji over the WebSocket without redactSecrets, another content path that bypasses credential masking.
failure_scenario: An agent sets its presence status to a string containing an ac_ token or claim URL (e.g. echoing an env var). set_status (lines 1759-1767) forwards status_text raw to the hub, which surfaces it to other members as presence — no redaction is applied, unlike the message-send paths. Lower blast radius than a channel message but still a member-visible credential leak.
suggested_fix: Apply redactSecrets(status_text) (and status_emoji if free-form) before dispatching the set_status frame.

summary: The @mention context budget is labeled/intended as a byte cap (maxBytes = 15_000, maxPerMsg = 2_000) but is measured with String.length (UTF-16 code units), not UTF-8 bytes.
failure_scenario: For CJK/emoji-heavy channels (common here — the code itself uses Chinese status notes), a Chinese character is 1 code unit but 3 UTF-8 bytes, so a 15,000-"byte" budget can carry ~45,000 actual bytes of context. The context prefix pushed to the model can be ~3x larger than the guardrail intends, defeating the small-context-model protection the comment describes; conversely an all-4-byte-emoji message is under-counted differently. The per-message 2KB clip has the same char-vs-byte skew.
suggested_fix: Measure with Buffer.byteLength(clipped, 'utf8') (or new TextEncoder().encode(...).length) for both totalBytes and the per-message clip so the cap reflects real wire/payload bytes.

summary: Inbound message handling calls data.content.slice(...) and data.sender_id.slice(...) without null-guarding, so a message frame lacking a content/sender_id field throws and aborts delivery.
failure_scenario: A `message` frame arrives for a DM (isDM true) or an active hidden-identity game (activeHi true) whose content is null/absent (e.g. an attachment-only or system-generated message). Line 3273 `data.content.slice(0, 50)` throws before the server.notification() call at 3277, so the outer try/catch logs the error and the message is never surfaced to Claude Code. The same unguarded slice on data.content/data.sender_id exists in the silent-channel branch at line 3297.
suggested_fix: Use optional chaining / defaults consistently: (data.content || "").slice(...) and (data.sender_id || "").slice(...), matching the guarded usage already present in get_history (line 2320) and the mention check (line 3188).

summary: Add tests for normalizeChannelDocLevel: integer 1-4 accepted, out-of-range/float rejected, 'L3'/'3' string forms parsed, garbage → null.
failure_scenario: Doc-level normalization gates channel doc filtering. A regression (e.g. accepting level 0 or 5, or failing to parse the `L`-prefixed string form) mis-buckets channel docs/skills so the wrong docs surface to the agent. Pure function, trivially testable, currently untested.
suggested_fix: Export and bun-test: 1/2/3/4 → same number; 0, 5, 2.5, NaN → null; '3' → 3, 'L3'/'l3' → 3, 'L5' → null, '' → null, non-string → null.

summary: Add tests for parseSkillFrontmatter covering the key allowlist, quote stripping, key normalization (argument-hint→argument_hint), and malformed frontmatter (no closing ---).
failure_scenario: Skill frontmatter parsing feeds save_skill/sync_skill metadata. If it regresses, a skill's name/description/trigger is dropped or a body without frontmatter is mis-sliced, so published skills surface with wrong or missing metadata. Edge cases untested: missing closing `---` must return the whole string as body with empty metadata; keys outside the allowlist must be ignored; `argument-hint` must map to `argument_hint`; single/double quotes stripped.
suggested_fix:
Export and bun-test: a valid `---
name: X
description: 'Y'
argument-hint: Z
---
body` yields metadata {name:'X',description:'Y',argument_hint:'Z'} and body 'body'; a non-`---` string returns {metadata:{}, body:input}; a `---` with no closing marker returns the input as body; an unknown key like `foo: bar` is excluded.

summary: Add tests for extractChannelDocsPayload / isSkillDoc / compactSkillDoc covering the three payload shapes, the skill-detection heuristic, and the id/doc_id + camelCase/snake_case field fallbacks.
failure_scenario: These three pure helpers normalize varied server doc payloads. isSkillDoc uses a loose heuristic (kind OR id-contains-'skill' OR title-contains-'skill') that can both false-positive (a normal doc titled 'skillful notes' treated as a skill) and false-negative; compactSkillDoc must fall back across id/doc_id and updatedAt/updated_at and skill_meta/skillMeta. A regression silently mis-lists or drops fields in list_skills output. Untested.
suggested_fix: Export the three and bun-test: extractChannelDocsPayload on a bare array, {docs:[...]}, {channel_docs:[...]}, and junk → []; isSkillDoc true for kind='skill'/'channel_skill' and for id/title containing 'skill', false otherwise; compactSkillDoc maps both naming conventions and reads meta from skill_meta and skillMeta.

summary: No tsconfig.json, no typecheck/lint script — 79 `: any` and TS errors go uncaught.
failure_scenario: No tsconfig.json exists in mcp-plugin (or root covering it) and package.json has no typecheck/lint/build script. The code is heavy TypeScript (`type: module`, 79 `: any`, 47 unchecked casts) but nothing ever type-checks it; type regressions and the pervasive `any` sprawl are invisible until runtime, and there is no editor/CI enforcement of strictness.
suggested_fix: Add a strict tsconfig.json, a `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` script (and eslint), and run it in CI.

summary: Inline `require("fs")` used 4x in an ESM (type:module) file that already imports readFileSync/writeFileSync at the top.
failure_scenario: Lines 2736, 2742, 2765, 2771 call `require("fs").readFileSync/writeFileSync`, but the same functions are already ESM-imported at line 34. In a `"type": "module"` package `require` is not defined under standard Node ESM (ReferenceError: require is not defined); it only works because the runtime is bun. This is both dead/inconsistent (duplicating already-imported symbols) and a latent break if the file is ever run under Node or bundled.
suggested_fix: Delete the `require("fs")` calls and use the already-imported readFileSync/writeFileSync.
